newsitem.title: UK: Whitbread says in talks with BrightReasons.
newsitem.headline: Whitbread says in talks with BrightReasons.

text.p: Brewer to leisure group Whitbread Plc confirmed on Friday it was in talks over the purchase from BrightReasons of its pizza and pasta restaurant chain.

Despite press reports that Whitbread is prepared to pay up to 90 million stg for the 180-strong chain, analysts say the company has valued it at no more than 50 million stg. "I don't think they are at all interested in the brands, (Bella Pasta, Pizza Piazza and Pizzaland), but they might see it as a good route to secure sites across the country, in other words as a purely real estate deal," said Mark Puleikis, analyst at Merrill Lynch.
"I do not think they are worth more than 300,000 stg a site and really Whitbread should see it as a way of gaining sites for their other brands like Costa Coffee or Cafe Rouge," he added.
Whitbread already owns Pizza Hut, Britain's largest pizza chain in a joint venture with PepsiCo.
"I have got nothing to add to the statement that has been issued," said a spokesman for Whitbread.

BrightReasons was put up for sale this month by venture capital groups, Morgan Grenfell and Mercury Asset Management, which hold some 86 percent of the company. Pizzaland was acquired by a management team led by Michael Guthrie from Grand Metropolitan five years ago, with venture capital backing.
